summary: Lithuania's crime register publishes suspects and victims of every offence, with sex and whether they are minors, but gives citizenship only for all offences together. The national trafficking review gives victims and suspects by citizenship. That is a citizenship proxy only; ethnicity (tautybė), including the Polish and Russian minorities, is not recorded in crime data.
european_title: Not recorded by any Lithuanian crime source
european_note: Lithuanian crime records hold citizenship, not ethnicity. Poles, Russians and other minorities are counted in the census but not in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Lithuania records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Offences against sexual freedom and inviolability (chapter XXI)
harms.intro: Chapter XXI offences had 186 suspects (22 minors) and 313 victims, 268 of them minors, in 2025; molestation of a child (Art. 153) had 71 suspects and 140 child victims. Citizenship is given only for all offences together (2025: 1,362 foreign and 278 stateless of 23,009 victims; 989 foreign and 74 stateless of 21,782 suspects).

breakdown.why: The Interior Ministry's IT department (IRD) publishes suspects and victims for each Criminal Code article with sex and minors (sexual-freedom chapter 2025: 186 suspects, 268 child victims), but citizenship only for all offences together (2025, natural persons: 989 foreign, 74 stateless of 21,782 suspects; 1,362 foreign, 278 stateless of 23,009 victims).
IRD's child-victim form gives 471 children who suffered physical violence in 2025, with no citizenship; citizenship exists only in the all-offence totals.
3 children recorded as suffering neglect in 2025 (IRD child-victim form) and 22 offences of abuse of parental authority, with no citizenship; only all-offence totals by citizenship.
Murder (Art. 129: 70 registered in 2025) has suspects and victims by sex and minors only; citizenship only in all-offence totals.

The 2025 national trafficking review (Seimas Ombudsmen, from IRD, prosecutor and police data) gives 62 victims, 1 of them a child; 92% were foreign citizens (mostly Sri Lanka and Uzbekistan). Of 19 suspects, 16 were Lithuanian citizens and 3 foreign (Ukraine, Belarus, Saint Barthelemy).
Child pornography offences (Art. 309 part 2: 353 registered in 2025) have no citizenship; only all-offence totals by citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Lithuania scores 11% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Its crime register publishes child victims and suspects for every offence, but citizenship only for all offences together; trafficking victims and suspects are given by citizenship. No ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

ird.name: Nusikalstamų veikų žinybinis registras: rodikliai (crime register indicators)
ird.publisher: Informatikos ir ryšių departamentas prie Vidaus reikalų ministerijos (Interior Ministry IT and Communications Department)
ird.records: Registered offences, suspects and victims by Criminal Code article with sex and minors; all-offence suspects and victims by citizenship; child victims by type of harm (form 50N).
ird.limitations: Citizenship only for all offences together; no ethnicity.

thb.publisher: Seimo kontrolierių įstaiga (Seimas Ombudsmen, national rapporteur)
thb.records: Trafficking victims by sex, age and citizenship; suspects by sex, citizenship and age.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
